cases.summary: [PM-37182] Resend "New Device Login Protection" email doesn't work
cases.description: ### Steps To Reproduce Precondition: Have any 2FA disabled for your BW account and the "New Device Login Protection" (NDLP) activated. And use an "unknown device" or incognito browser window for the following now (to trigger NDLP): 1. Go to https://vault.bitwarden.com 2. Log in with your email and master password. 3. The automatic NDLP email gets through (though console shows error 400). 4. Click on 'Resend'. ### Expected Result I should get another email (and no error message in the console?!). ### Actual Result I don't get another email (and the console throws error "401 Unauthorized"). ### Screenshots or Videos To make it unambiguous: I'm talking about emails containing verification codes in the context of: https://bitwarden.com/help/new-device-verification/ ### Additional Context I created that BW account only for testing this and will delete it. (so no worries about privacy / redactions) PS: And I read about that issue with the resend button for the first time here: https://www.reddit.com/r/Bitwarden/s/994fV4fE9O ### Operating System Windows ### Operating System Version 11 Home 25H2 Build 26200.8328 ### Web Browser Vivaldi ### Browser Version 7.9.3970.64 (Official Build) (64-bit) ### Build Version 2026.4.2 (BW US cloud account) ### Issue Tracking Info - [x] I understand that work is tracked outside of Github. A PR will be linked to this issue should one be opened to address it, but Bitwarden doesn't use fields like "assigned", "milestone", or "project" to track progress.

[PM-37182] Fix bug that prevents re-sending of NDV email

## 🎟️ Tracking

https://bitwarden.atlassian.net/browse/PM-37182
fixes https://github.com/bitwarden/clients/issues/20611

## 📔 Objective

In https://github.com/bitwarden/server/pull/5964/changes#diff-19ca62a64f34d8a3f432d8d76e1f578f5dc87d1ff2859eb789faf6ae41fb1c20, the method to send New Device Verification OTPs was changed to use the authenticated user principal, which does not have a user context on unauthenticated endpoints.  This caused any requests to return a `401` response to the client.

This change looks up by email instead.  The secret verification for both MP and OTP verifies that the email address matches the requestor/owner of the secret.
